concerns.text: Task T005a is marked `[P]` (parallel‑safe) but it produces raw network files that are required by T005b‑d. The subsequent loader tasks depend on the files created by T005a, so they cannot safely run in parallel.
Task T005b is also marked `[P]` yet it computes checksums for files downloaded in T005a and writes `data/checksums.txt`. This consumer must run after the producer T005a; the `[P]` tag is inaccurate.
Task T005c validates downloads performed in T005a and aborts on failure. It must execute after T005a; marking it `[P]` creates a false parallel‑safety claim.
Task T005d writes `state/data_availability.yaml` based on the count of raw files produced by T005a. It depends on T005a completing successfully, so it cannot be parallel‑safe.

User Story 2 (tasks T022‑T029b) depends on outputs from User Story 1 (metrics JSONs and `sim_results.json`). This violates the requirement that each US block be independently shippable and testable end‑to‑end.
User Story 3 (tasks T032‑T035) depends on regression artifacts produced in US 2, again breaking the independently‑shippable unit rule for user‑story groups.
